zones.what: Lifeboats are mounted at Deck 5; they obstruct the lower portion of the view from Decks 6, 7, and 8, with Deck 6 experiencing the most significant obstruction and the effect diminishing as you go higher.
zones.effect: On Deck 6, you look directly at or just over the boats—horizon is visible but the ocean view down is blocked; Deck 7 sees mostly over them with partial obstruction; Deck 8 has minimal interference.
zones.mattersTo: Matters greatly to guests who want an unobstructed ocean view or watch the water directly below; doesn't matter to those focused on horizon views, sunsets, or who spend little balcony time.

zones.what: Pool deck, Solarium, and outdoor leisure areas are located on Deck 12 directly above mid and aft sections of Deck 11.
zones.effect: Daytime noise from pool activities, deck furniture moving, and music; foot traffic and splashing sounds can carry through to balconies and inside cabins below.
zones.mattersTo: Light sleepers, those working during the day, or anyone sensitive to intermittent activity noise overhead; doesn't bother guests who are out exploring during pool hours.

zones.what: Blu restaurant (AquaClass dining) and Café al Bacio are on Deck 11 mid-ship, directly above Deck 10 mid cabins.
zones.effect: Occasional noise from restaurant service, chair movement, and kitchen activity during breakfast and dinner hours; generally quieter than pool deck but still present.
zones.mattersTo: Guests who are in their cabin during meal times and are sensitive to overhead activity; minimal impact for those dining out or exploring during those hours.

zones.what: Main dining room (Grand Epernay) is located on Deck 10 mid-ship, directly above Deck 9 mid cabins.
zones.effect: Noise from dining service, particularly during the two main dinner seatings—chair scraping, footsteps, service activity from approximately 6pm to 10pm.
zones.mattersTo: Early-to-bed guests or those in cabin during dinner hours; doesn't affect those dining out or at shows during evening hours.

zones.what: Main theater (Celebrity Theater) spans Decks 4 and 5 below forward and mid sections of Decks 7 and 8.
zones.effect: Show audio and bass can transmit upward during evening performances, typically 7pm-10pm; the effect diminishes with distance but is noticeable on Deck 7.
zones.mattersTo: Early-to-bed guests or those trying to relax in cabin during show times; doesn't affect night owls or those attending the shows.

zones.what: Fortunes Casino and Sky Conference Center are on Deck 11 directly below Deck 12 aft cabins.
zones.effect: Casino noise—music, slot machines, voices—can be heard in cabins above, particularly in evening hours when casino activity peaks.
zones.mattersTo: Light sleepers and those who retire early; doesn't bother guests who stay up late or enjoy the casino themselves.

zones.what: Elevator banks are located forward, mid-ship, and aft on all guest cabin decks, with the mid-ship bank being the primary vertical circulation hub.
zones.effect: Cabins adjacent to elevator lobbies experience door chimes, conversation, and foot traffic throughout the day and night; convenience is excellent but noise trade-off exists.
zones.mattersTo: Light sleepers and those sensitive to hallway noise should avoid cabins immediately adjacent to elevator banks; mobility-limited guests benefit greatly from proximity.

zones.what: Engine room and propulsion machinery are located low and aft, below and behind the aftmost cabins on Decks 3, 6, and 7.
zones.effect: Low-frequency vibration and hum are noticeable in aft cabins on these lower decks, particularly when engines are working hard during maneuvering or high-speed cruising.
zones.mattersTo: Guests sensitive to vibration or mechanical noise; doesn't bother those who sleep through ambient sounds or who value aft balcony wake views more than silence.

zones.what: Bow thrusters are located in the forward hull below the lowest guest decks.
zones.effect: Thruster noise—a loud rushing or rumbling—occurs during docking and departure maneuvers in forward cabins, particularly on lower decks; typically brief but intrusive when it happens.
zones.mattersTo: Light sleepers who are in cabin during early morning arrivals or evening departures; doesn't affect those who are up and out during port days.

zones.what: Anchor chain locker is located in the bow below Deck 3 forward cabins.
zones.effect: Loud metallic rattling and rumbling when anchor is dropped or raised, typically during early morning port arrivals; the noise is distinctive and can wake sleepers.
zones.mattersTo: Light sleepers in forward Deck 3 cabins on port-intensive itineraries; doesn't affect those who wake early anyway or who sleep through mechanical sounds.

zones.what: Crew access points and service corridors intersect with guest areas on Deck 3, particularly near the forward and mid sections where crew movement supports lower-deck operations.
zones.effect: Occasional crew traffic and service cart movement in early morning hours for cabin service prep and galley supply; brief but noticeable in adjacent cabins.
zones.mattersTo: Very light sleepers in Deck 3 cabins near crew access points; most guests won't notice or won't be bothered by brief, professional crew activity.

zones.what: AquaClass cabins on Decks 10 and 11 have exclusive access to the Persian Garden thermal suite and Blu restaurant, creating higher foot traffic in these corridors.
zones.effect: More hallway activity from spa-goers in robes during morning and evening hours; a different demographic mix and slightly more corridor noise than standard cabin decks.
zones.mattersTo: Guests seeking maximum hallway quiet may notice the difference; AquaClass guests value the exclusive amenity access and won't mind the traffic they're contributing to.

unknowns: Whether Solstice-class ships have a hump (balconies cantilevered past hull line) at all—I cannot confidently confirm the presence, location, or affected decks for this specific class without risking the error described.
Precise location and extent of galley noise impact—while galleys exist, their exact deck location and which cabins experience ventilation or service noise is uncertain.
Specific connecting cabin configurations beyond what's typical for the category mix shown—whether certain deck sections have higher concentrations of connecting doors.
